reviewNotes: HOLD / canonical-backstage. Current first-party top-up validity is usable for balance-lifecycle data, but the provider has a live 30-day-vs-180-day conflict in official expired-balance recovery wording and does not expose a clean number-recycling deadline. Preserve the conflict and do not reuse stale community lifecycle claims.

events.outcome: Current Cellcard official surfaces conflict on the post-expiry top-up recovery window: the English business/self-service terms say expired balance can be restored by top-up within 30 calendar days, while the current Khmer main-site terms state 180 days. Do not infer number-retention/recycling timing from either balance-recovery window until reconciled.

data.acquisitionSummary: Cellcard currently sells physical SIM and eSIM. Current get-SIM surface lists a free eSIM with AO MOBILE 5G plans starting at USD2/7 days; international travelers can also buy/activate a 5G eSIM through Cambodia eArrival. Exact generic bare-number fee is not assigned here.

keep.action: Current Cellcard top-up table gives USD50 a 180-day main-balance Active Period; smaller denominations give shorter periods. This supports a conservative roughly two-top-up-per-year balance-validity path, but the exact phone-number suspension/recycling lifecycle after Active Period expiry is not established and must not be equated with balance expiry.

data.chinaActivation: International-traveler eSIM acquisition is documented through Cambodia eArrival, but this review does not establish China-first activation or durable use from China.
data.kyc: Cellcard requires accurate subscriber profile/ID information; exact foreign-passport registration workflow for this generic route is not fully reconciled.
data.payment: Online top-up currently supports credit/debit card, Alipay, WeChat Pay and local bank methods.
data.roamingSms: unverified for long-term foreign OTP use
data.refund: Prepaid main balance is stated non-refundable.
data.holdReason: Current top-up Active Periods are clear, but provider surfaces conflict on expired-balance recovery (30 vs 180 days) and do not establish the exact number suspension/recycling lifecycle.
data.tariffSummary: Top-up validity currently ranges from 7 days at USD1 to 180 days at USD50; exact number lifecycle after balance expiry remains unresolved.
guideSteps: Acquire/register a current Cellcard SIM/eSIM using an official channel.
If preserving balance validity, use the current top-up validity table and renew before the Active Period ends.
Do not treat the 30-day or 180-day expired-balance recovery text as a confirmed phone-number recycling deadline until Cellcard reconciles the official-source conflict.
